name: Transfer list
purpose: Moves items between two labelled lists — 'Available' and 'Selected' — via checkboxes and move controls. Itinerary row 27 (P3, 'Move-between lists'), explicitly mapped to NOT be row 40's List-items ('⚠ NOT row 40's List-items (fuzzy matches on "list")'). Use where a user must build a subset FROM a larger set (assign accounts to a payee group, pick recipients for a standing instruction) and seeing both the chosen and unchosen sets at once matters more than a compact multi-select dropdown.
$status: PROPOSED #209, Dave's eye owed — new component, built through the gated-component route at #209 wave 3 lane B. Nothing about it is ruled.
$composesFrom: Two gated idioms, copied rather than re-drawn, per THE JOB's own instruction (List-items + Selection-controls idioms): (1) List-items supplies the row shell — the 44px+ row, the divider-between-items rhythm, the hover surface, the truncating single-line label with text-box-edge:text text so descenders aren't clipped. (2) Selection-controls supplies every checkbox verbatim, INCLUDING the panel-header 'select all' reusing the INDETERMINATE state exactly as Selection-controls' own 'Select all (indeterminate)' specimen does (same input.indeterminate JS toggle, same tick/mixed-dash SVG paths, same tokens). The ONE piece with no single-source precedent is the move-controls column and the cross-panel DOM move + role="status" announcement — authored for this component specifically (see behaviour).

props.name: availableItems
props.$note: Items shown in the left/'Available' panel. Each item is a checkable row (id + label).

props.name: selectedItems
props.$note: Items shown in the right/'Selected' panel — the outcome of the control.

props.name: checkedIds
props.$note: The currently ticked rows in EITHER panel — drives which items 'Move selected' acts on and which header checkbox shows checked/indeterminate/unchecked.

variants.name: default
variants.use: Two panels side by side with a four-button move column between them (single/all, both directions).

tokens.row: tertiary/background/hover on row hover — copied from List-items' own .row:hover treatment
tokens.divider: divider/border/section — between rows and under each panel header, copied from List-items
tokens.checkbox: form/border/default (unchecked border) / secondary/background/default (checked fill) / text/on-inverse (tick glyph) — copied byte-for-byte from Selection-controls' checkbox
tokens.moveButton: form/border/default border, icon/default glyph, tertiary/background/hover on hover, icon/disabled + border when the button has nothing to act on (empty panel or nothing checked)
tokens.label: text/default @ .t-cm-label (panel header) / .t-cm-caption (item count) / .t-cm-input (row label)
tokens.$note: NO NEW TOKEN IS WANTED OR MINTED. Every value already exists and is already bound by List-items or Selection-controls.

responsive.rule: Two panels + a move column in a flex row; below 480px (container query) the layout stacks to a single column with the move controls turned into a horizontal row between the panels. Verified at 1000px and inside a narrow container.

mustNotNeighbour: List-items used bare as a fake transfer list by pairing two independent List-items instances with no shared move mechanism — that reproduces this component's look without its behaviour

accessibility.checkbox: Native <input type="checkbox"> per row plus one per panel header, exactly as Selection-controls' own checkbox and indeterminate 'select all' idiom — no custom keydown was authored for selection itself.
accessibility.moveButtons: Four real <button>s, natively focusable and Enter/Space-activatable. Each carries a visually-hidden text description ('Move selected to Selected' / 'Move all to Available' etc.) via aria-describedby so meaning never rests on the chevron glyph alone (1.4.1) — the glyph is aria-hidden.
accessibility.liveRegion: Each panel owns its own role="status" (visually hidden) that announces '<n> item(s) moved to <panel>' after a move — authored specifically for this component; there is no List-items or Selection-controls precedent for announcing a cross-panel DOM move (4.1.3).
accessibility.focusManagement: NOT YET HANDLED after a move: focus currently stays on the move button, which is legal (the button did not disappear) but a screen-reader user gets no cue that their checked rows physically relocated beyond the status announcement. Flagged, not silently accepted — see $decisionsForDave.
accessibility.emptyPanel: An empty panel renders a text row ('No items') rather than a blank surface, and its header checkbox auto-disables (mirrors the 'no blank surface' rule List-items' processing/empty states already model).
accessibility.colourIndependence: Row/panel state never relies on colour alone — checked state is a filled glyph + a fill colour together (Selection-controls' own two-channel answer), and every count is a visible number, not a dot or bar.

antiPatterns: Moving DOM nodes without leaving each panel's header checkbox recomputed — a stale 'select all' state (checked when the panel is now empty, or vice versa) would silently lie to the next user action
A move button that stays enabled with nothing to act on (e.g. 'Move selected' enabled when nothing is checked) — this build disables each button against its own precondition
Relying on the chevron direction alone to convey which panel receives the moved items — every button also carries a text description

Building this as a single custom two-column widget with synthetic rows instead of composing List-items' row shell + Selection-controls' checkbox — that would re-draw idioms THE JOB explicitly said to copy

tokenValidation.result: PROPOSED — worker lane B build, #209. No gate has been run by this worker (conductor's serial set runs _validate_snippets.py / _validate_a11y.py / _validate_type_composites.py / _validate_radius.py / _validate_icons.py / _validate_coverage.py). This is a proposal, not a proof-of-done.
tokenValidation.$note: The four chevron glyphs are byte-matched paths from knowledge/assets/icons/arrows-and-chevrons/{chevron-right,chevron-left,chevron-double-right,chevron-double-left}.svg, referenced via <symbol>/<use> with an explicit fill="currentColor" on every <path> — the same <use>-shadow-tree fix Rating's meta records was caught and applied here too (a real render surfaced it: icons rendered solid black in both themes until the fill attribute was added, because a `svg path` CSS selector cannot reach into a <use> instance's shadow content).

provenance.$note: Itinerary row 27 (reviews/ITINERARY-STATUS-2026-08-19-v1.json), measured a TRUE GAP: all five signal probes negative on transfer-list, drift AGREES. Explicitly NOT row 40/List-items per the itinerary's own fuzzy-match warning.

$differsFrom.List-items: List-items rows are either informational or single-action (tap the whole row to navigate/act). This component's rows are CHECKABLE and the row itself does nothing on click — selection state, not navigation, is the point. The row SHELL is copied; the interaction model is not.
$differsFrom.Selection-controls (Checkbox): Selection-controls documents the checkbox atom in isolation, one field at a time. This component is the first place in the library where a checkbox's checked state is consumed by something OTHER than its own label — a cross-panel move — which is why the move mechanism had to be authored rather than found.

$decisionsForDave: After a move, should focus follow the moved item's new position in the destination panel, move to the panel heading, or stay on the move button (as built)? Dave's call — this is a genuine UX/AT trade-off, not a mechanical one.
Should there be a maximum item count per panel before it needs its own internal scroll/search (the max-height:280px overflow:auto on each <ul> is a placeholder cap, not a ruled one)?

Is drag-and-drop between panels wanted alongside the checkbox+button mechanism, or is checkbox+button the whole interaction surface by design (as built, itinerary note says only 'move-between-lists')?
